scope: Domain entities, value objects, and policies.
pass: PASS: domain imports only language or domain-local modules.
warn: WARN: an adapter boundary needs a documented translation.
fail: FAIL: domain code imports React, React Router, Supabase, or Drizzle.
exceptions: A pure type declared in a framework-agnostic shared package is acceptable after dependency review.
detection: Search domain imports for framework and infrastructure module names.
remediation: Move framework interaction to an adapter and pass a domain value or port.
validation: Inspect domain import graphs and confirm no forbidden package path reaches a domain module.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/features/* is separated from the external-adapter categories app/core/lib/*.server.ts and app/core/db/*.server.ts, corroborating a policy-to-adapter boundary without asserting import conformance.

scope: Route, application, domain, port, infrastructure, screen, and component dependencies.
pass: PASS: routes depend on application; application depends on domain and ports; infrastructure implements ports.
warn: WARN: a transitional adapter is documented with a removal path.
fail: FAIL: a lower layer imports a route, screen, component, or infrastructure implementation.
exceptions: A composition root may wire an infrastructure implementation to an application port.
detection: Trace imports from domain/application modules toward route and infrastructure paths.
remediation: Invert the dependency through a port or move composition to the route/server entry point.
validation: Inspect import edges and confirm routes→application→domain/ports while infrastructure only implements ports.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/routes.ts, app/features/*/screens, app/features/*/components, app/core/lib/*.server.ts, and app/core/db/*.server.ts are distinct categories.

scope: Cross-feature imports under app/features.
pass: PASS: another feature imports only the target feature's explicit public entry point.
warn: WARN: a temporary cross-feature import has an owner and removal issue.
fail: FAIL: one feature reaches another feature's internal route, component, or data module.
exceptions: Shared cross-cutting code may live in an intentionally shared core module.
detection: Search feature-to-feature relative imports that bypass a feature public index.
remediation: Export a narrow API from the target feature or relocate truly shared code.
validation: Inspect cross-feature import paths and confirm each ends at an explicit public API.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/features/{auth,blog,contact,cron,home,legal,payments,settings,users} are separate top-level ownership categories; the approved contract makes each feature's explicit entry point its cross-feature boundary.

scope: Feature structure and clean-architecture seams.
pass: PASS: layers exist only where they clarify a real policy, boundary, or change risk.
warn: WARN: a simple feature may stay flatter with its rationale visible in code.
fail: FAIL: ceremony obscures a needed boundary or a shortcut crosses a protected boundary.
exceptions: A small read-only feature may use a direct route-to-repository adapter when no domain policy exists.
detection: Inspect whether each layer owns a distinct policy, port, or adaptation responsibility.
remediation: Collapse empty abstractions or introduce the smallest boundary that protects policy.
validation: Inspect representative feature flows and confirm layers correspond to observable responsibilities, not class counts.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): screen-only features coexist with features that also have api, components, layouts, lib, or schema categories; the observed category sets vary and do not establish a universal layout.

scope: Business operations that coordinate domain policy and external effects.
pass: PASS: application use cases express intent and depend on named ports for external effects.
warn: WARN: a trivial operation may remain inline until it coordinates policy or multiple effects.
fail: FAIL: domain policy is coupled directly to a Supabase client, route request, or UI object.
exceptions: Read-only projection code may map a repository result without a separate use-case class.
detection: Search application/domain modules for direct framework client or request imports.
remediation: Introduce a narrow port and call it from an application operation.
validation: Inspect multi-step operations and confirm external effects are invoked through named application-facing ports.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/core/lib/*.server.ts and app/core/db/*.server.ts isolate external adapters, while features use varied category sets rather than a universal class, repository, or use-case template.

scope: Server modules that import filesystem, database, network, or vendor adapters.
pass: PASS: infrastructure modules own external I/O, serialization, vendor mapping, and infrastructure error translation only.
warn: WARN: a storage-specific compatibility normalization remains local and is explicitly not product or domain policy.
fail: FAIL: an infrastructure module also owns reusable domain decisions, application orchestration, or presentation tokens and defaults.
exceptions: Serialization helpers, vendor DTO mapping, storage-specific compatibility normalization, and infrastructure error mapping may remain beside the adapter.
A trivial read-only projection may map a row directly when it contains no reusable policy or presentation styling.
detection: Search modules importing node:fs, Supabase, Drizzle, database, network, or vendor clients for entity factories, ordering or state transitions, read-modify-write orchestration, fallback product policy, or CSS and Tailwind tokens.
remediation: Keep I/O and vendor mapping in infrastructure; move reusable factories and policy to a pure model or domain module, read-modify-write coordination to an application operation, and visual token mapping to presentation. Use functions unless a class or port isolates a real change reason.
validation: Inspect infrastructure module imports and exported behavior and confirm external I/O, serialization, and vendor error mapping remain without reusable domain policy, application orchestration, or presentation tokens.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): feature screen and component paths are distinct from feature api and query paths plus app/core/lib/*.server.ts and app/core/db/*.server.ts adapter categories; the approved contract defines responsibility purity without claiming every observed file conforms.

scope: Admin, customer, API, worker, and shared runtime entrypoints that participate in one product flow.
pass: PASS: each runtime surface has an explicit entrypoint and owner, dependencies point toward intentionally shared contracts, and the surfaces are independently traceable and verifiable.
warn: WARN: a small deployment shares one process while retaining explicit surface modules, dependency direction, and separate verification seams.
fail: FAIL: admin, customer, API, or worker responsibilities are mixed in one screen or module so a change cannot be traced or verified by surface.
exceptions: A prototype may use one deployable and one process; this rule requires responsibility boundaries, not microservices or separate deployments.
detection: Trace runtime entrypoints and cross-surface imports for mixed route, presentation, protocol, and privileged server responsibilities.
remediation: Create the fewest explicit entry modules and shared contracts that make ownership and dependency direction visible without forcing a new deployment topology.
validation: Inspect runtime entrypoint modules and the dependency graph and confirm admin, customer, API, and worker responsibilities have explicit owners without forbidden upward edges.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: user-facing screens, admin screens, route/API adapters, and shared rendering or domain code need distinct ownership even when they ship in one process.

scope: Starter routes, features, configuration, dependencies, and generated surface area reachable from the requested slice.
pass: PASS: reachable starter residue is either used by a named consumer or removed inside the authorized scope with verification.
warn: WARN: uncertain or out-of-scope starter residue is retained with its uncertainty, likely owner, and the evidence needed before removal.
fail: FAIL: confirmed unused starter routes, features, or dependencies remain in the delivered slice and falsely imply supported behavior.
exceptions: Never delete repository-wide code merely because it looks unused; dynamic imports, deployment tooling, and external routes require evidence and authority.
detection: Search route registries, import reachability, package scripts, runtime configuration, and build output for starter artifacts without a consumer.
remediation: Remove only confirmed dead residue inside the authorized slice, then re-run the same route, dependency, build, and behavior checks.
validation: Search route registries, dependency graphs, and build artifacts and confirm removed starter code has no runtime consumer while every retained residue has a named owner or uncertainty.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: unused template features should not be presented as implemented capability, but cleanup must stay within explicit scope and evidence.

scope: React Router route reads and rendered server data.
pass: PASS: a loader supplies route server data and the route consumes generated loader data.
warn: WARN: useEffect is limited to synchronizing an external client-side system.
fail: FAIL: a route fetches its own server data in an effect or copies loader data into local state.
exceptions: A client-only browser API may be synchronized in an effect after hydration.
detection: Search route and screen files for fetch effects and state initialized from loader data.
remediation: Move the read to a loader and retain useState only for ephemeral UI state.
validation: Inspect route reads and confirm server data originates in a loader rather than a mount-time effect.

scope: React Router mutations initiated by route UI.
pass: PASS: mutations use an action with Form or fetcher semantics.
warn: WARN: imperative submission is documented when a native form cannot express the interaction.
fail: FAIL: route mutations bypass action/Form/fetcher with ad-hoc client fetch state.
exceptions: A browser-only interaction with no server mutation may use local state.
detection: Search route UI for mutation fetch calls not connected to an action or fetcher.
remediation: Define an action and submit through Form or useFetcher.
validation: Inspect each server mutation and confirm it is represented by an action, Form, or fetcher.

scope: Route module loader, action, and component signatures.
pass: PASS: route modules use generated Route types for route arguments and data.
warn: WARN: a generated type gap is recorded next to a temporary explicit adapter type.
fail: FAIL: a route hand-rolls incompatible params or loader/action argument shapes.
exceptions: A framework-independent application input type may be defined separately from Route types.
detection: Search route modules for loader/action signatures lacking generated Route type references.
remediation: Regenerate route types and use the generated Route namespace at the adapter boundary.
validation: Inspect route module signatures and confirm loader/action/component contracts use generated route types where available.

scope: Loaders, actions, and server handlers that access protected data or effects.
pass: PASS: the server authenticates the caller and checks authorization before protected work.
warn: WARN: an intentionally public route states its public data and effect boundary.
fail: FAIL: a protected loader/action trusts client role state or omits server authorization.
exceptions: Public content may omit an identity check only when its repository operation is public by design.
detection: Search protected route handlers for session lookup and authorization policy before repository calls.
remediation: Authenticate on the server and enforce resource-level authorization before the effect.
validation: Inspect protected loaders/actions and confirm server identity plus authorization precede protected queries or mutations.

scope: Route responses, expected errors, and unexpected failures.
pass: PASS: expected statuses map to route UI and unexpected errors reach an ErrorBoundary.
warn: WARN: a shared boundary may render a documented generic recovery UI.
fail: FAIL: a route renders an unclassified exception as normal data or hides its status.
exceptions: A normal empty result is rendered as an explicit empty state, not an error boundary.
detection: Inspect route throws/returns and ErrorBoundary handling for status-to-UI mapping.
remediation: Return or throw a meaningful status and render it in the route error boundary.
validation: Trace representative empty, domain, and unexpected paths and confirm each reaches an explicit route state.

scope: URL params, search params, navigation, fetcher, and loader state.
pass: PASS: router-owned state remains in React Router APIs; useState holds only ephemeral UI state.
warn: WARN: a local draft mirrors a URL value only while an explicit edit interaction is active.
fail: FAIL: route code stores URL/search/navigation/fetcher or loader state as an unsynchronized duplicate.
exceptions: A transient input draft may differ from the committed URL until submission.
detection: Search for useState initialized from search params, navigation, fetcher, or loader values.
remediation: Read router state directly and keep local state only for temporary UI interaction.
validation: Inspect state ownership and confirm URL, navigation, fetcher, and loader data are not copied into persistent local state.

scope: Supabase client creation and credential use.
pass: PASS: browser, server session, and privileged admin clients are distinct and scoped.
warn: WARN: an admin client is isolated in a server-only module with a documented purpose.
fail: FAIL: a browser bundle can import a service-role client or client scopes are conflated.
exceptions: A server-only job may use an admin client after its execution boundary is verified.
detection: Search client factories and imports for service-role keys or server modules reachable from browser code.
remediation: Create separate browser, server, and admin factories and isolate privileged imports.
validation: Inspect client factory paths and confirm service-role credentials occur only in server-only admin construction.

scope: Supabase repository adapters and application-facing errors.
pass: PASS: repositories map provider failures to meaningful domain or application outcomes.
warn: WARN: an unmapped provider code is surfaced with context while a mapping is added.
fail: FAIL: Supabase error objects leak through application or UI boundaries without classification.
exceptions: A diagnostic server log may retain the original provider error as attached context.
detection: Search repository return types and throws for raw PostgrestError exposure.
remediation: Translate provider codes into named outcomes and preserve the cause only for diagnostics.
validation: Inspect repository error paths and confirm callers receive application-level error categories rather than raw client errors.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/features/auth/lib/queries.server.ts and feature queries.ts paths are separated from feature screens.

scope: Supabase query results crossing into application or domain code.
pass: PASS: infrastructure maps raw rows and nullability into application/domain values.
warn: WARN: a temporary raw projection is confined to a repository with a removal note.
fail: FAIL: UI or domain code branches on raw Supabase row shape or relation payloads.
exceptions: A repository may return a deliberate read-model DTO owned by the application boundary.
detection: Search screens and domain modules for Supabase generated row type imports.
remediation: Map the result inside the repository and return a named application model.
validation: Inspect query consumers and confirm raw database response shapes stop at infrastructure adapters.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): feature query paths and feature screens/components are separate categories, providing a mapping seam without prescribing a repository class.

scope: Typed Supabase database access.
pass: PASS: queries use generated Database types and update them when schema changes.
warn: WARN: an unsupported query helper isolates a precise local type with a generation follow-up.
fail: FAIL: database access replaces generated types with broad casts or invented row types.
exceptions: A mapped application DTO may intentionally differ from the generated database row.
detection: Search Supabase client creation for Database generics and casts around query results.
remediation: Regenerate Database types and type the client with the generated schema.
validation: Inspect Supabase client construction and confirm query typing originates from generated database types.

scope: Supabase Realtime subscriptions in client UI.
pass: PASS: a subscription is created for a stable key and removed during cleanup or key change.
warn: WARN: a long-lived provider documents its ownership and teardown boundary.
fail: FAIL: a component creates subscriptions without deterministic removal.
exceptions: A process-level server listener may outlive a component when its shutdown hook removes it.
detection: Search channel subscriptions for matching removeChannel, unsubscribe, or cleanup functions.
remediation: Return cleanup from the owning effect or centralize lifecycle management in a provider.
validation: Inspect each subscription creation and confirm a deterministic cleanup runs on unmount or key replacement.

scope: Database schema, function, grant, and policy changes.
pass: PASS: schema-affecting changes are represented by ordered migrations under version control.
warn: WARN: a local experiment is discarded or promoted to a migration before shared use.
fail: FAIL: production schema behavior depends on dashboard-only or manual untracked changes.
exceptions: An ephemeral local test database may be reset from tracked migrations.
detection: Compare schema-related code changes with the migration history and deployment instructions.
remediation: Add a reversible, ordered migration and regenerate dependent types where needed.
validation: Inspect schema, policy, function, and grant changes and confirm each has a committed migration artifact.

scope: Postgres tables, privileges, and Supabase exposed data.
pass: PASS: exposed tables enable RLS and grants permit only required roles and operations.
warn: WARN: a documented service-only table is inaccessible to browser roles.
fail: FAIL: user-reachable data lacks RLS or grants exceed the operation's least privilege.
exceptions: A non-exposed internal table may omit RLS only with restricted privileges and a documented boundary.
detection: Inspect migrations for ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, policies, and GRANT statements.
remediation: Enable RLS, add ownership-aware policies, and revoke unnecessary grants.
validation: Inspect every exposed table's migration and confirm RLS policy plus minimum role grants protect its operations.

scope: Postgres functions callable through the application or API.
pass: PASS: functions set a safe search_path and use deliberate invoker/definer privileges with narrow grants.
warn: WARN: a migration documents why elevated execution is required and its callable roles.
fail: FAIL: a callable function has unsafe name resolution or broad execution privileges.
exceptions: A private maintenance function may be ungranted to application roles but still sets its search path.
detection: Inspect CREATE FUNCTION migrations for search_path, SECURITY mode, and GRANT EXECUTE.
remediation: Set a secure search_path, choose privilege mode explicitly, and restrict execute grants.
validation: Inspect each application-callable function and confirm search_path and execution grants are explicitly constrained.

scope: Postgres views exposed to application roles.
pass: PASS: each exposed view deliberately uses and reviews security_invoker behavior with its underlying policies.
warn: WARN: a legacy definer view is documented with owner, grants, and migration plan.
fail: FAIL: an exposed view bypasses intended table policy through unreviewed security semantics.
exceptions: An internal owner-only reporting view may be unavailable to application roles.
detection: Inspect CREATE VIEW migrations for security_invoker and the grants/policies of referenced tables.
remediation: Set security_invoker where appropriate or document controlled definer ownership and grants.
validation: Inspect each exposed view and confirm its security_invoker or deliberate alternative is reconciled with underlying RLS.

scope: Operations that must persist multiple related database changes together.
pass: PASS: all-or-nothing multi-write work uses a transaction or single RPC boundary.
warn: WARN: independently recoverable writes document their compensation and partial-success UI.
fail: FAIL: required related writes can leave an invalid partial state after an intermediate failure.
exceptions: An asynchronous outbox write may occur after the committed transaction when retries are idempotent.
detection: Trace multi-step mutation flows for a transaction, RPC, or explicit compensation boundary.
remediation: Move the related writes into one transaction or a database RPC with clear failure semantics.
validation: Inspect invariant-preserving multi-write operations and confirm one atomic transaction or RPC encloses them.

scope: TypeScript source and declarations.
pass: PASS: uncertain values are unknown and narrowed with a real guard or schema.
warn: WARN: a third-party declaration gap is isolated behind a typed adapter while upstream typing is pursued.
fail: FAIL: explicit any erases a value's contract in application code.
exceptions: Generated or vendor files may retain any outside application ownership and are not re-exported as app contracts.
detection: Search owned TypeScript for ': any', '<any>', and 'as any'.
remediation: Replace any with unknown, a union, a generic, or a validated boundary type.
validation: Search owned TypeScript and confirm explicit any is absent from maintained application contracts.

scope: TypeScript suppressions and assertions at unsafe boundaries.
pass: PASS: an assertion follows runtime proof and a suppression names the verified upstream limitation.
warn: WARN: a narrow, documented interop assertion is paired with a runtime guard.
fail: FAIL: @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, non-null, or broad assertion hides an unvalidated unsafe value.
exceptions: A compile-time exhaustive-check assertion may be used after the union is narrowed.
detection: Search owned code for ts-ignore, ts-expect-error, non-null assertions, and broad casts.
remediation: Validate the value, model the union, or isolate documented interop behind an adapter.
validation: Inspect each suppression or assertion and confirm a preceding runtime proof or narrow documented interop boundary exists.

statement: no server code through client barrels
scope: Public index files and browser-reachable imports.
pass: PASS: client-facing barrels export only browser-safe modules; .server code stays server-reachable only.
warn: WARN: a shared type-only export is verified to erase from runtime output.
fail: FAIL: a client import can reach a .server module, secret, or server client through an index barrel.
exceptions: A server-only barrel may export server modules when it is itself unreachable from client routes.
detection: Trace barrel exports from client routes and screens for .server paths or server client imports.
remediation: Split server and browser entry points and export shared types with type-only imports.
validation: Inspect client-reachable index exports and confirm no import path reaches a .server module or server credential client.

scope: Request, environment, webhook, provider, and persisted untrusted inputs.
pass: PASS: unknown input is parsed by Zod before it becomes an application input or domain value.
warn: WARN: a trusted internal call documents the prior validating boundary.
fail: FAIL: untrusted input crosses into application or domain logic without validation.
exceptions: A value constructed by a validated schema in the same flow need not be parsed again.
detection: Trace unknown request/provider/environment values to their first schema parse.
remediation: Define a Zod schema at the boundary and pass its parsed output inward.
validation: Inspect every trust boundary and confirm unknown input is parsed with Zod before application/domain use.

scope: Application input types validated by Zod.
pass: PASS: TypeScript input types use z.infer from the schema that validates them.
warn: WARN: a DTO adds a documented derived field after parsing.
fail: FAIL: a parallel hand-written input interface can drift from its validation schema.
exceptions: A domain value type may be narrower than the parsed transport input after construction.
detection: Search schemas for matching manually declared input interfaces.
remediation: Export z.infer<typeof Schema> and derive any domain value after parsing.
validation: Inspect validated input types and confirm the caller type is inferred from the exact Zod schema used at the boundary.

statement: do not repeatedly parse trusted data
scope: Already validated application and domain values.
pass: PASS: parsed values retain their trusted type through the same internal flow.
warn: WARN: revalidation occurs at a new trust boundary such as serialized storage or a queue.
fail: FAIL: internal code repeatedly parses the same trusted value to compensate for unclear ownership.
exceptions: Data decoded from an external cache or process boundary is untrusted again and must be parsed.
detection: Search repeated schema.parse calls on values already typed as that schema output.
remediation: Carry the parsed type inward and parse again only after a new untrusted boundary.
validation: Trace parsed values through one operation and confirm additional parsing happens only after serialization or external ingress.

scope: React component render functions.
pass: PASS: reusable or stateful child components are declared at module scope.
warn: WARN: a tiny render helper may stay local when it is not a component and captures no lifecycle.
fail: FAIL: a component definition is nested in render and remounts or obscures ownership.
exceptions: A pure local formatter returning markup may remain local when it is not used as a React component.
detection: Search component bodies for capitalized function declarations or component arrow assignments.
remediation: Hoist the child component or extract a cohesive module with explicit props.
validation: Inspect render bodies and confirm capitalized React components are module-scoped rather than defined during render.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): reusable UI lives in app/core/components and app/features/*/components instead of the route registry category.

scope: Presentation components and screen-to-component contracts.
pass: PASS: the screen maps route or application data into explicit semantic props or a cohesive named view model, and components render that contract.
warn: WARN: a short-lived single-use leaf accepts a presentation-ready feature model and names the consumer or variation that would trigger a narrower contract.
fail: FAIL: a reusable or item-varying component hardcodes product or route-specific copy, status, options, or CTA; imports a persistence record as its UI contract; reaches hidden data; or infers semantic state by parsing display strings.
exceptions: Stable component-owned chrome or accessibility copy may remain local when it never varies by item, route, permission, or release state.
A presentation component may map a semantic variant such as sale or forest to CSS classes locally.
detection: Inspect reusable components for item-specific literals, release dates, version options, CTA policy, raw persistence types, CSS tokens carried by data models, index-based semantic state, and comparisons or includes calls against display labels.
remediation: Have the screen map validated route or application data into a presentation-ready named view model; pass varying copy, options, status, CTA, and semantic visual variants as explicit values, then let components map those values to markup and CSS.
validation: Inspect two representative screen view models and confirm displayed copy, options, status, CTA, and visual variants come from semantic props without item-specific component literals, persistence shapes, or display-label parsing.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/features/*/screens and app/features/*/components are separate presentation categories.

statement: index is explicit public API only
scope: Feature and component index modules.
pass: PASS: an index exports a deliberate small public surface.
warn: WARN: a temporary compatibility export lists its consumer and removal condition.
fail: FAIL: an index wildcard-exports internals or accidentally exposes server-only implementation.
exceptions: A package root may re-export a curated set of stable modules.
detection: Inspect index files for export stars and internal/server implementation paths.
remediation: Replace blanket exports with named public exports and split server entry points.
validation: Inspect index files and confirm each export is intentional, consumer-facing, and browser-safe where applicable.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/features/* directories are feature boundaries; no index.ts path was treated as evidence of runtime behavior.

scope: Feature screen modules.
pass: PASS: a screen arranges view models and presentation components without data fetching or persistence.
warn: WARN: a screen may contain small display-only mapping near the composed component.
fail: FAIL: a screen directly queries infrastructure, owns route protocol, or embeds domain policy.
exceptions: A screen may receive already prepared loader data and callbacks as explicit inputs.
detection: Search screen modules for Supabase clients, route request APIs, and business policy branches.
remediation: Move adaptation to the route/application layer and pass a view model into the screen.
validation: Inspect screen imports and confirm they compose presentation rather than fetch, mutate, or enforce domain policy.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/routes.ts and feature api paths are distinct from app/features/*/screens presentation paths.

scope: React UI state and React Router state.
pass: PASS: ephemeral UI uses useState, external synchronization uses useEffect, and router state uses router APIs.
warn: WARN: a custom state abstraction documents the lifecycle it improves.
fail: FAIL: state is duplicated across framework ownership boundaries without synchronization.
exceptions: An isolated state machine may own a complex local interaction with a clear input/output boundary.
detection: Inspect hooks that mirror router data or use effects for ordinary derived UI state.
remediation: Use the framework-native owner and derive values during render where possible.
validation: Inspect state variables and confirm each is owned by React local UI, an external synchronization, or React Router as appropriate.

scope: Admin previews and customer-facing rendering of the same published view model or SDUI contract.
pass: PASS: preview and customer surfaces use the same renderer or shared rendering core over the same validated view model.
warn: WARN: surface-specific chrome wraps one shared renderer and parity is checked on representative fixtures.
fail: FAIL: preview and customer rendering duplicate component selection or transformation logic that can drift independently.
exceptions: Surface-specific navigation, controls, and diagnostics may differ outside the shared published content boundary.
detection: Compare preview and customer render paths for duplicated switch statements, mappings, view-model transforms, or component registries.
remediation: Extract one rendering core or component registry and feed both surfaces the same validated fixture or published view model.
validation: Run a preview parity test with one validated view model and confirm the admin preview and customer renderer produce the same semantic component tree.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: a preview exists to represent the customer result, so duplicated renderers are an operational drift risk.

scope: Styles reachable by multiple routes, bundles, features, or admin and customer surfaces.
pass: PASS: styles have an explicit owner through modules, a feature namespace, a component boundary, or another verified scoping mechanism.
warn: WARN: a deliberate global utility or design token is documented and tested across all reachable surfaces.
fail: FAIL: generic global selectors with different definitions can be loaded together and alter another surface unintentionally.
exceptions: Intentional resets, tokens, and utilities may be global when their contract is singular and documented.
detection: Search reachable stylesheets and built CSS for duplicate global selectors with conflicting declarations across surface owners.
remediation: Adopt CSS Modules, an explicit feature namespace, a component scope, or one canonical shared global definition.
validation: Search the browser bundle and component stylesheets and confirm reachable global selectors do not collide across admin and customer ownership.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: separately authored admin and customer styles can enter one global bundle and must not share accidental class ownership.

scope: User-visible outcomes from reads and mutations.
pass: PASS: outcomes are explicitly normal empty, expected domain, recoverable external, or unexpected system.
warn: WARN: an ambiguous provider failure is temporarily shown as recoverable external with diagnostics.
fail: FAIL: a user-visible failure is flattened into an unclassified null or generic success path.
exceptions: A normal empty collection is a first-class non-error state.
detection: Trace repository and route failure returns to their rendered state category.
remediation: Introduce named outcome types and map each category to a deliberate UI response.
validation: Inspect representative outcomes and confirm empty, domain, external, and system paths each render distinct semantics.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/core/screens/404.tsx and app/core/screens/error.tsx are distinct from route and feature screen paths.

statement: no swallowed errors or fake success
scope: Catch blocks, fallback chains, and mutation responses.
pass: PASS: caught errors retain a classified outcome and failed mutations do not report success.
warn: WARN: a documented degraded read state remains visible with its cause logged safely.
fail: FAIL: catch returns [] or null, ignores the error, or claims an effect succeeded when it failed.
exceptions: A normal not-found result may map to an explicit empty state after verified classification.
detection: Search catch blocks for empty bodies, return []/null, and unconditional success responses.
remediation: Classify the failure, show a bounded recovery state, and preserve diagnostic context.
validation: Inspect catch paths and confirm each produces a classified outcome rather than a silent fallback or fake success.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): app/core/screens/error.tsx is separate from feature query and server-client paths, preserving an explicit failure-presentation seam.

scope: Retries, degraded external dependencies, and recovery UI.
pass: PASS: fallback is visible, retry attempts are bounded, and retried effects are idempotent.
warn: WARN: a non-idempotent effect offers an explicit user-confirmed retry path instead of automatic retry.
fail: FAIL: hidden fallback chains retry indefinitely or repeat a non-idempotent mutation.
exceptions: A read-only cache fallback may be automatic when stale state is clearly labeled.
detection: Inspect retry loops, catch fallbacks, and mutation retry behavior for bounds and idempotency keys.
remediation: Expose degraded state, cap retries, and add idempotency or require explicit confirmation.
validation: Trace fallback behavior and confirm users can see it, attempts are bounded, and automatic retries are idempotent.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): explicit 404 and error screens exist as visible presentation categories rather than hidden data defaults.

scope: Automated tests for changed product behavior.
pass: PASS: tests target meaningful risk, policy, integration, or regression value with the smallest sufficient scope.
warn: WARN: low-risk presentation behavior may rely on focused manual verification when automated value is low.
fail: FAIL: a material behavior change lacks a justified verification path.
exceptions: Generated code and third-party behavior need not be re-tested by application tests.
detection: Inspect changed behavior against tests and identify the risk or regression each test covers.
remediation: Add the smallest test that proves the important behavior or document a focused verification reason.
validation: Inspect changed behaviors and confirm each material risk has a proportional automated or explicit verification method.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): e2e/auth, e2e/settings, and e2e/users organize verification by user risk area.

scope: Test suite design and assertions.
pass: PASS: each test proves product behavior, a boundary contract, or a real regression risk.
warn: WARN: a snapshot is retained only when a reviewer can name the visual or structural contract it protects.
fail: FAIL: tests only exercise libraries, private call counts, meaningless snapshots, or mock choreography.
exceptions: A narrow adapter contract test may assert an externally required call shape.
detection: Inspect assertions for user-observable behavior rather than implementation call counts or mock sequences.
remediation: Replace implementation-detail tests with a focused behavior or boundary contract assertion.
validation: Inspect representative tests and confirm each assertion maps to a product risk, boundary contract, or prior regression.
plate_evidence: Plate 8449384cdfad30f20337bad6536b0c7d46a3dde5 path category observation (structure only): e2e tests are grouped under auth, settings, and users behavior categories; this observation establishes no coverage or snapshot quota.

scope: Changes that affect routing, bundling, runtime entrypoints, deployment configuration, or claims of deployable readiness.
pass: PASS: the declared production build succeeds and the actual built artifact serves the critical path in a smoke check.
warn: WARN: a low-risk non-deployable prototype explicitly limits its claim to development mode and records the missing artifact check.
fail: FAIL: deployable or production-ready completion is claimed from a development server alone, or the built artifact cannot serve the critical path.
exceptions: A documentation-only or pure-library change may use a narrower verification path when no deployable artifact is affected.
detection: Inspect package scripts and deployment configuration, then compare development checks with the command that creates and serves the production artifact.
remediation: Run the declared build, serve or execute its output in the target-compatible runtime, and smoke the smallest critical route and failure path.
validation: Run the declared production build and smoke test the built artifact, then confirm the critical route responds from that artifact.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: a working development server is not evidence that the deployment artifact can boot or serve the product flow.

scope: New or retained production dependencies and their reachable browser or server bundles.
pass: PASS: each runtime dependency protects a named boundary, removes justified repeated implementation, or supplies required platform behavior, and its reachable cost is inspected.
warn: WARN: an existing dependency is retained for compatibility with a named removal trigger and no new consumer is added.
fail: FAIL: a runtime dependency is added or retained for one trivial internal constant or unused path without a named boundary, consumer, or comparative build evidence.
exceptions: Development-only tooling may be justified by repeatable verification or generation even when it does not ship at runtime.
detection: Inspect package and lockfile diffs, import reachability, and build output for new or unused runtime dependencies.
remediation: Use an installed fit-for-purpose dependency at a real boundary, replace trivial use with platform or TypeScript primitives, or remove the unused package and re-build.
validation: Inspect the dependency graph and bundle diff and confirm each added runtime dependency protects a named boundary or removes justified repeated implementation.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: dependency choice is an engineering tradeoff; a library installed for one trivial local value creates cost without boundary value.

scope: New stateful or durable agent workloads when Cloudflare Workers and the Agents SDK are compatible with task constraints and installed capabilities.
pass: PASS: compatible agent workloads use the Cloudflare Agents SDK for durable identity and state, and use Workflows or agent execution primitives according to duration and recovery needs.
warn: WARN: an incompatible event or runtime uses an explicit adapter seam and records why Cloudflare Agents SDK cannot be used.
fail: FAIL: a compatible project that selected Cloudflare Agents SDK bypasses it with an ad-hoc in-process agent loop that loses required state, recovery, or observability.
exceptions: Do not install or force Cloudflare infrastructure when the event, deployment target, time budget, or existing stack forbids it.
detection: Inspect agent entrypoints, state ownership, workflow duration, retry needs, and installed Cloudflare bindings before selecting the runtime.
remediation: Use Agent for durable identity and interaction, Workflows for retryable multi-step execution, and an adapter boundary when the target runtime differs.
validation: Inspect agent and workflow entrypoints and confirm the selected Cloudflare runtime or documented adapter matches state, duration, recovery, and task constraints.

scope: Multi-agent generation, review, ranking, acceptance, and repair workflows.
pass: PASS: producer agents and judge roles are separated, the judge reads immutable candidate evidence, and deterministic tests or policy gates own final acceptance where possible.
warn: WARN: a single-agent workflow exposes uncertainty and remains subject to independent deterministic verification because parallel judging adds no proportional value.
fail: FAIL: the same generation result approves itself from confidence alone, or a judge can silently mutate the candidate it claims to assess.
exceptions: Do not add multiple agents merely to increase agent count; one producer plus deterministic verification is preferable when independent perspectives add no material evidence.
detection: Trace candidate production, judge inputs, mutation permissions, verdict evidence, and the final acceptance gate.
remediation: Give producer and judge distinct roles, pass immutable candidate artifacts and criteria to the judge, preserve dissent, and require deterministic checks for executable claims.
validation: Trace the producer and judge workflow and confirm the judge reads immutable evidence, cannot silently mutate the candidate, and cannot replace deterministic acceptance tests.
plate_evidence: Junho Plate review-derived contract: AI-generated candidates require an independent evidence boundary, while deterministic policy and verification remain the final acceptance authority.

scope: Environment secrets, service-role credentials, and privileged tokens.
pass: PASS: secrets are read only in server-reachable modules and never serialized to browser output.
warn: WARN: a public browser key is labeled public and carries no elevated privilege.
fail: FAIL: a secret or service-role credential is imported, embedded, or exposed to client code.
exceptions: Public publishable configuration may reach the browser only after privilege review.
detection: Search client bundles, route data, logs, and environment access for secret variable names and service keys.
remediation: Move secret use into a server-only module and pass only a minimal authorized result to the client.
validation: Inspect browser-reachable imports and serialized loader data and confirm no secret or service-role value can reach them.

scope: Every protected resource read, mutation, remote effect, and destructive operation.
pass: PASS: authorization is enforced on the server against the requested resource and action.
warn: WARN: a UI permission hint may improve UX but is not treated as enforcement.
fail: FAIL: client role checks are the only gate for a protected server operation.
exceptions: Public operations may omit authorization only when their server repository policy is intentionally public.
detection: Trace protected actions from UI through route/server handlers to authorization policy checks.
remediation: Add server resource-level authorization before query, mutation, or remote effect execution.
validation: Inspect protected server handlers and confirm resource-level authorization occurs before the protected operation.

scope: External sends, purchases, deletes, privileged changes, and irreversible actions.
pass: PASS: the user gives explicit, informed consent immediately before a remote or destructive effect.
warn: WARN: a reversible draft may prepare an effect but cannot execute it without confirmation.
fail: FAIL: code performs a remote or destructive effect without explicit user consent or approved server automation authority.
exceptions: A documented server automation may execute only within its pre-approved scope and audit trail.
detection: Trace effect triggers for a confirmation intent, consent record, or approved automation identity.
remediation: Add an explicit confirmation step and server-side scope check before execution.
validation: Inspect each remote or destructive trigger and confirm explicit consent or documented automation authority precedes execution.
